question: Do official project records identify a DOST-funded Paco/Concordia biodiversity study or expose the fish results behind Orozco and Tolentino's 2015 AABE abstract?

recordsReviewed.citation: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development. (2010). PCIEERD Annual Report 2010. Department of Science and Technology, p. 19.
recordsReviewed.finding: Under the Pasig River Stewardship Program's ongoing work, the report lists a Far Eastern University project titled Physicochemical and Biodiversity Study of Estero de Paco. It says the work includes Estero de Concordia and uses physicochemical and biological parameters intended to provide baseline information.

recordsReviewed.citation: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development. (2011). PCIEERD Annual Report 2011. Department of Science and Technology, Table 2A, pp. 25-26.
recordsReviewed.finding: Table 2A is headed completed DOST-GIA R&D projects and lists the Pasig River Stewardship Initiatives with Project 5, Physico-chemical and Biodiversity Study of Estero De Paco. The parent program entry names DOST-ITDI and the U-Belt Consortium as implementers. The table gives no fish outcomes or underlying project report.

recordsReviewed.citation: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Environmental Management Bureau. National Water Quality Status Report 2006-2013, printed p. 48.
recordsReviewed.finding: The report attributes a Physicochemical and Biodiversity Study of Estero de Paco to Far Eastern University and summarizes its scope as ecological study, physical/chemical and biological parameters, temporal and seasonal variation, and assessment of pollution effects on biodiversity. It supplies no fish names, station results, or project data table.

recordsReviewed.citation: Far Eastern University. (2015). President's Report 2015, Faculty Presenters in International Conferences.
recordsReviewed.finding: The report lists Glorina Orozco presenting Limnological study of Esteros de Paco and de Concordia at the AABE 25th Conference in Kuala Lumpur, October 13-16, 2014. This independently cross-checks conference title and event metadata.

recordsReviewed.citation: Orozco, G. P., & Tolentino, M. S. (2015). Limnological Study of Esteros de Paco and de Concordia. Abstract presented at the 25th Biennial Conference of the Asian Association for Biology Education; Asian Journal of Biology Education, 8, 31.
recordsReviewed.finding: The publisher abstract supplies three fish-name labels and ecological summaries, but not the project award identifier, a DOST funding acknowledgment, full methods, collection dates, or the underlying station-level dataset.

lineageAssessment.2010To2011: The reports establish a temporal program context: an FEU Paco/Concordia biodiversity project is listed as ongoing in 2010, while a broader Pasig River Stewardship initiative that lists the Paco biodiversity project appears in the 2011 completed DOST-GIA table. They do not provide a project number, exact completion date, final report, or fish data.
lineageAssessment.abstractToDostProject: The 2015 AABE abstract has the same institution and Paco/Concordia focus as the project record. The reviewed materials do not explicitly state that the abstract is a DOST-funded deliverable; treat this as a plausible but unconfirmed relationship, not a proven publication lineage.
lineageAssessment.separateFromSanMiguelQuiapo: The Paco/Concordia abstract names different waterbodies from the Orozco-Zafaralla 2008/2012 San Miguel/Quiapo records. No merger or single-survey lineage is inferred.

queries: Exact project-title searches for Physicochemical and Biodiversity Study of Estero de Paco
Exact abstract title and Orozco/Tolentino author searches
FEU and DOST project-title searches for a final report or fish table
accessSearch.results: The bounded searches located the DOST annual reports, the EMB program summary, FEU's conference-presenter listing, and the AABE proceedings abstract. No publicly retrievable full project report or fish-by-station table surfaced.
accessSearch.limit: This search was bounded and cannot establish that a report, archive copy, or dataset does not exist.

decision.reason: Official records clarify the historical project and conference context but expose no additional fish data and do not prove the abstract's funding lineage.

nextActions: If an author or institutional archive response becomes available, request the final project report or fish-by-station annex and reuse terms; no request is sent by this review.
Preserve the existing three abstract labels only as historical research leads until a full table, methods, taxonomic basis, collection period, and station mapping can be checked.
Continue the NCR freshwater/brackish source review; NCR and Luzon baselines remain incomplete.
